properties.description:
Who a messaging channel belongs to.

WORKSPACE is a shared company number managed by someone with
``workspace.manage``. PERSONAL belongs to exactly one member and has **no**
implicit admin or owner access. Mirrors ``mail_backend.MailAccountScope``
deliberately — the two integrations answer the same ownership question and
must not drift (see docs/decisions/2026-07-27-mail-integration.md).

properties.description:
How much the agent may do on its own in one conversation.

The gate sits between the agent run and the provider call: AUTO sends the
reply, MANUAL does not run the agent at all (so an unattended conversation
costs no credits). Human review happens through the thread interrupt, not
through a channel-level draft — see
docs/decisions/2026-08-29-channel-drafts-removed.md.

operations.description:
List the user's agent runs that are working or waiting for approval.

Waiting runs sort first: they are the only rows a person can act on.
A run whose heartbeat expired is treated as crashed and omitted rather
than reported as still working. `search` matches the thread title and
summary; `activity` narrows to working or waiting runs.
operations.name: list-activity

operations.description:
List the user's active-workspace threads, filtered and ordered.

`pinned=true` returns only pinned threads, newest pin first whatever
`sort` says; `pinned=false` leaves them out, so the two lists never
show a thread twice.
operations.name: list

operations.description:
Mark the thread's answers as seen, so the list stops showing it unread.

A write of its own rather than a side effect of the interactions GET,
which stays safe to repeat and is limited as a read. A thread with
nothing unread is not written.
operations.name: mark-read

properties.description: The user message to go back before. It and what followed it stay as a version; the next message is written beside it.
properties.name: interaction_id

operations.description:
Go back to just before a user message, as `/rewind` does.

The thread then ends before that message and the model is back in the
state it was in then. The message and what followed stay reachable as a
version of it; nothing is deleted. Returns the messages as
`/interactions` does.
operations.name: rewind

operations.description:
Show another version of a message, and what follows from it.

`interaction_id` is the version to show: one of the message's
`sibling_ids`. The thread then continues from that version's first
answer, as Claude does, and returns its messages as `/interactions` does.
operations.name: select-interaction-version

operations.description:
Share the thread with its workspace as it stands now.

The link shows the messages up to now; later ones stay private until the
thread is shared again, which moves the snapshot and keeps the link. A
thread without messages is refused with `THREAD_EMPTY`.
operations.name: share

properties.description:
Scheme that wraps a container or file key for one member's public key.

The browser seals and opens every wrap; the server only stores the label.
`hpke-base-x25519-sha256-aes256gcm` is HPKE Base mode (RFC 9180) with
DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM.
properties.name: algorithm

`hpke-base-x25519-sha256-aes256gcm` is HPKE Base mode (RFC 9180) with
DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM.
properties.name: algorithm

operations.description:
Return the public half of a one-shot challenge keypair.

The browser answers it with the secret only the unsealed vault private key
derives, and resealing requires that answer. Without it a session that was
taken over could overwrite — and so destroy — key material it cannot read.
operations.name: create-reseal-challenge

operations.description:
Return a single secured file's key, wrapped for the caller.

Only for a file secured on its own. Inside a secured folder the container
key wraps the file, and that key is fetched for the folder instead.
operations.name: get-file-key

operations.description: Return the secured folder's key, wrapped for the caller's public key.
operations.name: get-folder-key

operations.description:
Return the signed-in user's vault keypair material.

The private key comes back sealed: usable only after the browser derives
the wrapping key from the vault passphrase or the recovery code.
operations.name: get-key

properties.description: Key-agreement algorithm of a user's vault keypair.
properties.name: algorithm

properties.description: Function that turns the vault passphrase into the wrapping key.
properties.name: kdf

operations.description:
Replace the sealed copies of the private key after a passphrase change.

PUT rather than PATCH: every sealed copy is rewritten together, and a
partial update would leave the recovery copy openable by the old
passphrase.
operations.name: reseal-key
